messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: service latency anomaly detected on /v1/generate — p95 increased beyond SLO. Pager delivered to oncall Priya Rao.

Priya Rao: I'm oncall and acked the page. Seeing spike in synthetic monitors and customer reports about sluggish responses. Kicking off traces and perf captures.

Ethan Kim: Pushed APM view: p50 jumped from ~45ms -> 160ms, p95 from ~120ms -> 520ms over last 18m. Traces attribute long tail to long-blocking syscalls (epoll_wait + io_getevents). No obvious CPU runaway in userland.

Margaret Li: Repro host logs show a flurry of NVMe queuing and multiple `io_submit` durations >150ms. Paste snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] req=tx-9f0a stage=serve host=inf-14 io_submit=162ms
[2026-03-15T21:12:04Z] req=tx-9f0b kv_cache_miss=true
```

Simone Carter: Correlated span timeline: request -> model-serve -> kv lookup -> fallback IO. KV miss ratio for route jumped from 2% -> 28% at incident onset. Could be cache TTL flapping or eviction thrash.

Luis Alvarez: Perf counters for affected node: context-switches spiked x3, softirq increased, rcu stalls seen in dmesg. Collected `perf.data` and BPF output.

Priya Rao: Immediate mitigations: 1) divert heavy customers to alternate cluster with warm cache, 2) enable smaller model variant for non-critical traffic, 3) temporarily increase IO scheduler deadline to reduce tail. Implementing now.

deploy-bot: @Margaret Li applied config change: route_fallback_model=small-llama-v2 on service/inference-group (deploy id dpl-90410).

Ethan Kim: I performed a controlled reboot to revert to previous kernel (6.2.11 -> 6.2.9) on one canary node. After reboot, same workload shows p95 back to ~130ms and syscalls normalized.

Margaret Li: Noted that a kernel rollout finished ~40m before the incident. Also saw a cache-ttl tweak in a deploy 35m prior. Autoscaler packed more pods onto fewer hosts around the same time -> densification might have amplified IO contention.

Simone Carter: Hypotheses (working list):
- H1: kernel regression in IO path (new kernel scheduling/driver interactions) causing long blocking syscalls.
- H2: recent cache-ttl change led to cold-cache storms -> bursty synchronous IO under packed placement.
- H3: combination: kernel change reduced tolerance for brief IO bursts, exposing latent behavior.

Luis Alvarez: Uploaded artifacts: `perf.data`, `bpf-trace.log`, `dmesg.txt`, and filtered kernel oops/warnings to https://s3.redwood.internal/2039876543/artifacts/ (ARTIFACT: use this prefix when adding more).

Priya Rao: Timeline draft: 20:25 kernel fleet rollout completed; 20:30 cache-ttl deploy; 20:48 first alert from monitors; 20:52 pager; 21:00 perf/traces show syscall tail; 21:10 mitigations applied; 21:18 canary kernel rollback; 21:28 canary stable.

Ethan Kim: Canary nodes (3) remain stable after kernel rollback. Raised infra ticket to pause kernel rollout across region. Also capturing before/after perf counters for formal comparison.

Margaret Li: Short action list:
- rollback cache-ttl change for affected shard (Margaret)
- coordinate full kernel fleet pause + bisect plan with infra (Ethan + Luis)
- keep impacted customers on alternate cluster and record exact timestamps for billing/credit assessment (Priya)
- collect contiguous perf traces and annotate traces with host-level counters (Simone)

Priya Rao: Oncall handoff plan: I'll hand to Margaret at 22:00 UTC for night watch. Please update this thread with any new artifacts. I'll start drafting the initial incident summary for #postmortems and customer comms.

Simone Carter: For RCA, we should capture: host perf pre/post, kernel dmesg, nvme driver version, placement maps showing pod packing, and the exact deploy that changed cache-ttl. I'll prepare a checklist in the runbook.

Luis Alvarez: Note: observed RCU stall messages in dmesg around 20:50 on a few hosts. Might be symptom rather than root cause, but I'll include them in the artifact bundle.

inc-bot: UPDATE: mitigation in place, tail latency improving. Next automated update in 30m or on change.

Priya Rao: Thanks all. If you add logs, prefix with ARTIFACT: so SRE can find them easily. We'll reconvene in the morning to finalize RCA and decide permanent remediation (kernel rollback vs driver patch vs placement change).
